Here is What to Know Beyond Why Arista Networks, Inc. (ANET) is a Trending Stock
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:00 AM CDT 5 min read
Arista Networks (ANET) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.
Over the past month, shares of this cloud networking company have returned -11.2%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +1.5% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Arista Networks falls in, has gained 0.8%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?
While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.
Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.
Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.
For the current quarter, Arista Networks is expected to post earnings of $1.08 per share, indicating a change of +44% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged over the last 30 days.
For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $4.12 points to a change of +38.3% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.
For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.12 indicates a change of +24.3% from what Arista Networks is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.
With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Arista Networks.
The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:
12-month consensus EPS estimate for ANET
Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.
For Arista Networks, the consensus sales estimate for the current quarter of $3.31 billion indicates a year-over-year change of +43.5%. For the current and next fiscal years, $12.63 billion and $16 billion estimates indicate +40.3% and +26.7% changes, respectively.
Last Reported Results and Surprise History
Arista Networks reported revenues of $3.04 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +37.7%. EPS of $1.02 for the same period compares with $0.73 a year ago.
Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.83 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +7.14%. The EPS surprise was +14.61%.
The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.
No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.
Comparing the current value of a company's valuation multiples, such as its price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), to its own historical values helps ascertain whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, whereas comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of how reasonable its stock price is.
As part of the Zacks Style Scores system, the Zacks Value Style Score (which evaluates both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics) organizes stocks into five groups ranging from A to F (A is better than B; B is better than C; and so on), making it helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.
Arista Networks is graded F on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.
The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Arista Networks. However, its Zacks Rank #2 does suggest that it may outperform the broader market in the near term.

Arista Networks Advances 4% While Ciena Soars 11% on AI Networking Demand; Cisco Rises 3%
Three networking and optical stocks are surging well past the broader market today, but the gaps between their gains reveal something specific about where AI infrastructure demand is hitting a wall.
Published October 6, 2026, 12:56pm ET · 4 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.

AI networking demand is lifting Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET | ANET Price Prediction), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Ciena (NYSE:CIEN), with shares of the optical supplier pulling far ahead of the two switching vendors. No company announcement accounts for the gain in Arista stock, which sits inside a broader bid across networking and optical equipment. That leaves the relative size of the three moves as the clearest signal of where the market sees demand outrunning supply.
Ciena stock is at $431.18, up 11% in midday trading, the largest gain of the three by a wide margin. Meanwhile, Arista Networks stock is at $214.34, up 4%, the smallest advance in the group. Cisco stock trades at $115.83, up 3%, landing between the other two.
For context, the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 0.63%, a modest gain for the broader tech sector. At the same time, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.76%. Against those benchmarks, shares of Ciena, Arista and Cisco are each running well ahead of both the tech sector and the overall market, a sign that the buying is targeted at network equipment.
Bernstein Note Ties Networking to Optical
On October 1, Bernstein initiated coverage of Arista Networks with an Outperform rating and a price target of $250, arguing that networking and optical suppliers both benefit from AI infrastructure spending, with demand still running ahead of supply. That note is several days old and serves as background to the session. The detail that matters now is the note’s pairing of networking with optical, since shares of Ciena, the optical name in this group, are running hardest.
Arista Networks reported its second-quarter 2026 results in early August, with revenue growth of 37.7% from a year earlier. Demand across AI networking, data centers, campus and routing drove that growth, giving the company several engines working at once, and such breadth underpins Arista’s longer-term story, though the August report isn’t fresh news for the stock and doesn’t explain the latest buying on its own.
Transport Layer Shows Where Scarcity Sits
Inside data centers, Arista and Cisco sell the switches and routers that move traffic, while Ciena supplies the optical transport layer that carries traffic between those facilities. A buildout that adds computing capacity in more locations lifts transport demand before it lifts switching demand. That sequencing is the structural reason Ciena, Arista and Cisco shares don’t move in lockstep, even when the same AI theme is driving all three.
Ciena stock running several times harder than Arista stock points to the transport layer as the place where the market currently sees scarcity. Bernstein’s note collapsed exactly that distinction by grouping networking and optical suppliers together under one spending thesis. Arista stock is the smallest mover of the three, which complicates reading the session as a story about Arista itself.
Between those extremes, Cisco stock is advancing solidly, which suggests the bid extends across the equipment layer as a whole. The middle slot held by Cisco stock also gives the market a useful reference point, since a broad rally lifts the diversified networking giant while the sharpest gains collect in optical transport. Such a pattern fits a market rewarding AI infrastructure broadly. It reserves its biggest premium for the scarcest piece (we profiled seven of these non-chip AI suppliers, from networking to power and cooling, in a free report you can grab here).
Evidence that switching demand is tightening the way transport demand appears to be would tie the next move in Arista stock to the company specifically, and this session doesn’t supply it. Traders could look for signs that Arista faces the same supply pressure Bernstein described across networking and optical suppliers. Until then, Ciena stock remains a clearer expression of the transport scarcity the market is pricing.
Shareholders may want to keep an eye on whether Cisco stock continues advancing alongside Ciena and Arista, since a sustained broad rally would support the view that AI networking spending is lifting every tier of the equipment stack. A fade in CSCO stock while CIEN stock holds its gains would point to a narrower trade concentrated in optical transport. Either outcome may clarify whether the equipment rally has staying power beyond the optical names.
Ciena stock carries the most risk of the three if transport scarcity eases, since it is running so far ahead of the group, while Arista and Cisco shares are riding the same spending wave with smaller swings. Investors weighing their exposure should calibrate their holdings carefully given that a sector-wide bid across networking and optical equipment is driving all three stocks. Keeping their positions in any one of these names moderate limits how much their portfolios lean on a single tier of the AI networking buildout.

Arista Networks (ANET -0.96%) is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings on Nov. 3, but I think the most important numbers in the report won't have anything to do with the third quarter.
Instead, I'll be watching what management says about the final three months of 2026.
According to Yahoo Finance, Wall Street expects the artificial intelligence (AI) networking company to generate $3.6 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and earnings of $1.15 per share. Those are some pretty ambitious targets, but I think Arista has a good chance to exceed them.
And if management delivers guidance that beats those expectations, I think Arista stock could soar after Nov. 3.
Image source: Getty Images.
Arista has become an important supplier of the high-speed networking equipment that connects processors and servers inside massive artificial intelligence data centers.
Companies such as Nvidia are developing increasingly powerful graphics processing units (GPUs), but those chips can't reach their full potential unless enormous amounts of information can move between them quickly.
Arista makes Ethernet switches that help eliminate networking bottlenecks, allowing thousands of processors to work together on demanding AI applications.
The company reported second-quarter revenue of $3.03 billion, a 37.7% increase from a year ago. Diluted earnings per share reached $0.95, compared with $0.70 in the year-earlier period. Management also projected third-quarter revenue of approximately $3.3 billion.
That's in line with what Wall Street projects. According to Yahoo Finance, the consensus Q3 estimates are $3.33 billion in revenue and $1.08 in earnings per share (EPS).
I'm not too worried about Q3 results -- instead, I'd rather look ahead. Investors already know that Arista is growing quickly. What they need to know now is whether demand for their networking equipment will remain strong as cloud computing companies continue to expand their AI infrastructure.
That's why fourth-quarter guidance could be more important than the third-quarter results themselves.
Market capMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary.$230.74B
Arista's path to topping Wall Street expectations
Arista has been introducing new networking products designed to handle increasingly demanding AI workloads.
Its 7060XE7 platform supports connections running at 1.6 terabits per second, while its recently announced Etherlink SU-144 architecture can connect up to 144 AI accelerators within a single-hop network.
Those capabilities are becoming more important as AI data centers grow larger and companies look for ways to get more performance from their expensive processors.
The opportunity is substantial, but so is the competition. Nvidia and Cisco Systems are also pursuing the AI networking market, and Arista depends heavily on spending by major cloud computing companies. Still, I think the company's recent growth gives management a reasonable opportunity to surprise Wall Street.
Arista typically provides quarterly revenue and margin guidance rather than an explicit earnings-per-share forecast. So I'll be watching whether its fourth-quarter revenue outlook exceeds $3.6 billion and whether its projected profitability supports earnings above the $1.15 consensus estimate.
A revenue forecast above expectations would suggest that demand for Arista's networking equipment remains stronger than Wall Street anticipated. Healthy margins would make that growth even more valuable to shareholders.

Here's Why Arista Networks (ANET) Could be Great Choice for a Bottom Fisher
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 7:55 AM CDT 3 min read
Shares of Arista Networks (ANET) have been struggling lately and have lost 12% over the past week. However, a hammer chart pattern was formed in its last trading session, which could mean that the stock found support with bulls being able to counteract the bears. So, it could witness a trend reversal down the road.
While the formation of a hammer pattern is a technical indication of nearing a bottom with potential exhaustion of selling pressure, rising optimism among Wall Street analysts about the future earnings of this cloud networking company is a solid fundamental factor that enhances the prospects of a trend reversal for the stock.
What is a Hammer Chart and How to Trade It?
This is one of the popular price patterns in candlestick charting. A minor difference between the opening and closing prices forms a small candle body, and a higher difference between the low of the day and the open or close forms a long lower wick (or vertical line). The length of the lower wick being at least twice the length of the real body, the candle resembles a 'hammer.'
In simple terms, during a downtrend, with bears having absolute control, a stock usually opens lower compared to the previous day's close, and again closes lower. On the day the hammer pattern is formed, maintaining the downtrend, the stock makes a new low. However, after eventually finding support at the low of the day, some amount of buying interest emerges, pushing the stock up to close the session near or slightly above its opening price.
When it occurs at the bottom of a downtrend, this pattern signals that the bears might have lost control over the price. And, the success of bulls in stopping the price from falling further indicates a potential trend reversal.
Hammer candles can occur on any timeframe -- such as one-minute, daily, weekly -- and are utilized by both short-term as well as long-term investors.
Like every technical indicator, the hammer chart pattern has its limitations. Particularly, as the strength of a hammer depends on its placement on the chart, it should always be used in conjunction with other bullish indicators.
Here's What Makes the Trend Reversal More Likely for ANET
An upward trend in earnings estimate revisions that ANET has been witnessing lately can certainly be considered a bullish indicator on the fundamental side. That's because empirical research shows that trends in earnings estimate revisions are strongly correlated with near-term stock price movements.
The consensus EPS estimate for the current year has increased 0% over the last 30 days. This means that the Wall Street analysts covering ANET are majorly in agreement about the company's potential to report better earnings than what they predicted earlier.
If this is not enough, you should note that ANET currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. And stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #1 or 2 usually outperform the market. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Moreover, a Zacks Rank of 2 for Arista Networks is a more conclusive indication of a potential trend reversal, as the Zacks Rank has proven to be an excellent timing indicator that helps investors identify precisely when a company's prospects are beginning to improve.

Thu, October 15, 2026 at 3:21 PM CDT 4 min read
Arista Networks has ridden a powerful multi year rally in cloud and AI networking, and after such a strong run the question is whether the cash the business can generate really supports where the stock trades today. With investors now weighing fresh AI product news against a recent pullback, the focus tightens on what its cash flows can justify rather than just what the share chart shows.
Over the past 5 years, Arista stock has risen by roughly 7x, which puts a lot of expectations about future cash generation under the microscope.
Recent AI focused rack scale networking launches and expectations for higher AI related revenue can support stronger and potentially more durable cash flows if customers keep building out large scale infrastructure on Arista hardware.

Does Arista Networks Look Fairly Valued on Cash Flow?
The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here is built on Arista Networks' ability to keep turning its networking position into cash over time. Over the last twelve months the business produced about $5.2b in free cash flow, which anchors the whole exercise. The projections then assume that free cash flow keeps growing into the early 2030s, reaching a level above $11b by 2030 in the base case, before easing into a slower phase after that.
Those assumptions point to a company that the model treats as a strong cash generator rather than a turnaround story, and on that basis the DCF suggests an intrinsic value broadly in line with the current share price of $195.42. The recent launch of rack scale AI architectures, built with large chip and hyperscale partners, helps explain why the market is comfortable paying a price that already reflects robust long term cash generation. Arista Networks vs. Axon Enterprise: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 10:16 PM CDT 6 min read
As cloud computing and public safety technology evolve, investors are weighing high-growth infrastructure against defensive software ecosystems. Choosing between Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) and Axon Enterprise (NASDAQ:AXON) requires balancing different risk profiles.
Arista provides high-speed networking equipment that powers modern data centers, while Axon dominates the law enforcement technology market through Taser devices and software. Both companies benefit from secular trends in automation and digitization, making them compelling candidates for growth-oriented portfolios looking for market leaders in their respective categories.
Arista Networks is a prominent player among tech stocks that design high-performance networking platforms for large-scale data centers. Its solutions are vital for artificial intelligence workloads that require massive bandwidth and low latency. The company primarily serves cloud titans and specialty providers. In its latest annual report, filed for 2025, customer concentration remained a key factor. Two major end customers accounted for 16% and 26% of revenue, respectively. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business if spending patterns shift.
In 2025, revenue reached $9 billion, representing approximately 29% year-over-year growth. The ongoing build-out of infrastructure for generative artificial intelligence drove this expansion. The company reported net income of roughly $3.5 billion for the period. Its net margin, which measures how much profit is retained from every dollar of sales, was close to 39%.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio stands at approximately 3.0x. This metric indicates the company has $3 in current assets for every $1 in short-term liabilities, suggesting strong liquidity. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating the company has no debt relative to shareholders' equity. Free cash flow, which is cash from operations minus capital expenditures, was roughly $4.3 billion.
Axon Enterprise specializes in hardware and cloud-based software for public safety agencies. Its ecosystem includes Taser energy devices, body-worn cameras, and digital evidence management systems. Unlike its peer, Axon has a diverse customer base, with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of net sales in 2025. The company is increasingly focused on its software-as-a-service offerings, which provide recurring revenue streams from law enforcement and federal agencies.
In 2025, revenue reached close to $2.8 billion, a significant 33.5% increase over the prior year. This growth highlights the increasing adoption of cloud software and next-generation safety devices. However, the company reported net income of approximately $125 million, resulting in a net margin of roughly 4.5%. This lower net margin reflects heavy investments in research and development to stay ahead of technological shifts.
According to its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.6x. This indicates that total debt is 60% of shareholders' equity. The current ratio, a measure of a company's ability to pay short-term debts, is roughly 2.5x.
Free cash flow was approximately $75 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 300% of operating cash flow, meaning this non-cash add-back heavily inflates reported cash generation.
Arista Networks faces revenue concentration risk, as a few large cloud and AI customers drive a significant share of its sales. The company also relies heavily on Broadcom for switching chips, making it vulnerable to supply chain disruptions. Competitive pressure from Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Extreme Networks creates persistent pricing pressure. Furthermore, geopolitical tensions and trade controls concerning China affect its global manufacturing operations and costs.
Axon Enterprise is dependent on law enforcement budgets, which can be affected by political shifts or economic constraints. The company also faces persistent risks from product liability and legal claims related to the use of its Taser devices. Rapid technological change requires constant innovation in AI and machine learning, which carries high research costs. Additionally, the company reported a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting as of Dec. 31, 2025, related to revenue recognition.
Investors must choose between Arista Networks, which trades at a lower Forward P/E, and Axon Enterprise, which has a significantly lower P/S ratio.
Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.
The Forward P/E compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.
Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Arista and Axon are both quality growth stocks to consider for the long term, but Axon is the stock I would buy right now. This is after the stock has fallen over 50% from its 2025 all-time high, providing an attractive entry point to invest in this dominant technology provider for law enforcement.
Arista is consistently posting high-double-digit revenue growth and will likely continue to do so, given the strong tailwinds in AI infrastructure spending. But Axon is posting equally impressive growth, as it pivots to providing AI-powered software. The company reported seeing robust demand last quarter, with 70% year-over-year growth in its software business.
Arista is generating higher margins, but this is largely priced into the stock's valuation. Analysts expect Arista's earnings to grow at an annualized rate of about 18% in the coming years. Its forward P/E of 44 puts the PEG ratio at over 2x.
Axon is expected to deliver 39% annualized earnings growth, with the stock trading at a forward P/E of about 53x, as of Oct. 20, 2026. That's a more attractive PEG multiple of 1.36x.
These are both solid growth stocks, but Axon is potentially the more undervalued, making it the one I would buy now.

•Delivered 40% growth in non-GAAP EPS year-over-year as the company achieved its first $3+ billion revenue quarter.
•Recognized on the 2026 Fortune 500 list of the largest United States corporations by revenue and named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Enterprise Wired and Wireless LAN.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. - August 4, 2026 -- Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET), an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large AI, data center, campus, and routing environments, today announced financial results for its second quarter ended June 30, 2026.
“As we deliver our first $3 billion quarter in Q2 2026, it is clear that our Arista 2.0 platform strategy is compelling,” stated Jayshree Ullal, Chairperson and CEO of Arista Networks. “Customers see networking as the central nervous system for infrastructure from the client to campus to data and AI centers.”
•Revenue of $3.036 billion, an increase of 12.1% compared to the first quarter of 2026, and an increase of 37.7% from the second quarter of 2025.
•GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 45.4% and 49.9%, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 44.7% and 48.8% in the second quarter of 2025.
•GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.95 and $1.02, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.70 and $0.73 in the second quarter of 2025.
A reconciliation of the company’s non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures has been provided in the financial statement tables included in this press release.
Commenting on the company's financial results, Chantelle Breithaupt, Arista’s CFO, said, “Our second quarter 2026 reflects strong, broad-based growth, with revenue up 37.7% and EPS up 39.7%. This performance underscores the strength of our market position and the continued dedication of our global team."
•Defending the Keys to the Kingdom: Resilient Infrastructure vs. AI-Capable Adversaries – Join Arista, Anthropic and Palo Alto Networks for a webinar to discuss the future of security in an AI world. Register here: https://events.arista.com/webinar-defending-the-keys-to-the-kingdom.
•Arista Networks was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Enterprise Wired and Wireless LAN – The recognition reflects Arista's continued momentum in the enterprise campus, built on its unified, single-EOS architecture spanning the data center to the campus edge.
•Arista introduced the 7060XE7 Series, a next-generation 1.6-terabit portfolio for AI fabrics – The new Etherlink™ platforms deliver up to 100 Tbps of system bandwidth and support Linear Pluggable Optics, cutting interconnect power consumption by approximately 60% compared to traditional pluggable optics.
•Arista detailed new innovations for scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across AI fabrics – The company outlined techniques including multi-planar leaf-spine designs, the open Multipath Reliable Connection
(MRC) protocol, and segment routing over IPv6 (SRv6), aimed at maximizing AI cluster utilization and resilience.
For the third quarter of 2026, we expect:
•Non-GAAP operating margin of 48 - 49%; and
•Non-GAAP diluted net income per share between $1.06 and $1.08.

The actual amount of these exclusions will have a significant impact on the company's GAAP gross margin, operating margin, and net income per share.

The financial results conference call will also be available via live webcast on Arista's investor relations website at https://investors.arista.com/. Shortly after the conference call concludes, a replay of the audio webcast will be available on Arista’s investor relations website.

The biggest risk is that AI buildouts or U.S. data center permitting slow while Arista has already locked in multiyear chip and memory commitments, which could leave utilization and gross margin under pressure. The Etherlink SU-144 scale up architecture is the announcement that matters most here because it goes straight to the core AI catalyst for Arista Networks. By extending Ethernet into tightly coupled accelerator domains of up to 144 XPUs per rack and over 1,000 XPUs across racks, the firm is trying to stay aligned with the way large customers design AI clusters. That same launch also highlights the execution swing factors. Liquid cooled, 100 kW plus racks, UEC based fabrics, and support for multiple scale up protocols increase Arista's footprint but require heavy up front commitments and integration work. If hyperscalers moderate AI capital spending or shift toward more in house solutions, this expanded ESUN and Etherlink stack could take longer to absorb than current plans assume. Photo: HaeB / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
On 19 October 2026, Judge Simon Birt at the High Court dismissed two claims against Uber totaling about £340 million. About 13,000 black cab drivers sought nearly £200 million and a Kabbee and Iride claimant about £140 million. Filed in 2024, the suits alleged Uber misled Transport for London to obtain its 2012 private-hire licence and diverted business from traditional operators. Uber denied the allegations. Birt found the claimants had access by February 2018 to information that could have enabled a case and ruled the claims time-barred under the six-year limit. He did not decide whether the allegations were true.
An Uber spokesperson said the court dismissed all of the claims entirely at the earliest opportunity and put these legacy matters firmly in the past. RGL Management, running the claimants' case, said it was very disappointed and is considering all options available to the claimant cab drivers with the legal team. Mishcon de Reya notified Uber by letter in 2019 then went silent four and a half years after a litigation funder withdrew. Outlets differ on the headline sum, with some citing £250 million ($333 million) and others about $453 million. On Sept. 9, the California Public Employment Relations Board certified the California Gig Workers Union as the bargaining organization for drivers working for covered transportation network companies. More Than 100,000 California Drivers Could Be Affected
The Transportation Network Company Drivers Labor Relations Act, which took effect Jan. 1, 2026, gives rideshare drivers the right to organize and bargain collectively while retaining their status as independent contractors.
For this all to happen, at least 30% of active drivers had to authorize the union to act as their bargaining representative. After reaching the 10% level in June, support topped the threshold required for certification by August. This led to formal certification by the PERB on Sept. 9.

A union might fight for workers’ rights, but it doesn’t mean the Uber and Lyft drivers will automatically get raises or new benefits. The ultimate financial effect on drivers, if any, will depend on the union’s course of action and what it can get companies to agree to.

California Is Testing a Different Model for Gig Work
The bigger story may be the unusual combination California has created.
The state has traditionally separated independent contractors from traditional employees for legal purposes. But this new system allows drivers to remain independent contractors while still potentially benefitting from the collective bargaining rights of the union.
As this is all somewhat experimental, it’s worth watching to see how it all plays out in California and whether similar approaches succeed elsewhere in the country. A strong collective bargaining agreement for Uber and Lyft drivers could ultimately alter the economics of rideshare driving for people who rely on these gig jobs for either supplemental income or full-time earnings. Whether or not any agreements alter the pricing structure for riders is also a worthy consideration.
For the time being, nothing about a driver’s paycheck will change immediately simply because the union was certified. But with the earnings of more than 100,000 active California rideshare drivers potentially being affected, these new developments mark a significant change for one of America’s best-known gig-economy jobs.

| Photo Credit:
Uber Technologies has agreed to acquire US workplace catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion in an all-cash transaction, as the ride-hailing and food delivery company seeks to expand Uber Eats into group catering and workplace meals.
Uber, in a press release on Tuesday, said that the acquisition will combine ezCater’s catering and business-to-business expertise with Uber Eats’ consumer and restaurant network and Uber for Business’ relationships with organisations, the companies said in a joint announcement.
ezCater enables businesses to order food from more than 140,000 restaurants across the US and manages workplace meals, meetings, events and recurring catering requirements. The platform generated more than $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the trailing 12 months, growing at a high-teens rate year-on-year.
The business is profitable on a non-GAAP operating income basis and is expected to be margin accretive to Uber, according to the companies. Its average order value exceeds $400, significantly positioning catering as a higher-value segment for restaurants and delivery partners.
Uber sees catering as a major revenue opportunity
“Catering is a big business, and can be a huge revenue stream for restaurants,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said, adding that Uber’s reach could bring ezCater’s catering experience to more customers and help restaurants capture more such orders.
The transaction is expected to provide restaurants with access to larger orders and new customers, while allowing consumers to order food for workplace gatherings, events and social occasions through a more integrated platform. Uber also expects the deal to create additional earning opportunities for its delivery couriers.
ezCater CEO Nihad Rahman said the company would bring its catering and B2B expertise into Uber’s broader ecosystem of customers, merchants and couriers.
Uber expands food delivery beyond individual meals
The acquisition comes as Uber looks to broaden its food delivery business beyond individual meal orders. By combining ezCater’s established workplace catering platform with Uber Eats’ existing consumer and restaurant reach, the company expects to expand access to group food orders while strengthening the value proposition for restaurant partners.
The transaction is expected to close in the coming months, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.
J.P. Morgan Securities is serving as financial adviser to Uber, while Evercore is advising ezCater. Covington & Burling and Freshfields US are providing legal counsel to Uber, while Davis Polk & Wardwell is advising ezCater.

Uber-ezCater deal: Why Uber is spending $2.3 billion on corporate catering
Uber will buy ezCater for $2.3 billion to expand corporate catering, grow Uber Eats and strengthen its delivery business with high-value orders.
Uber Technologies said on Tuesday that it will buy US corporate catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion in an all-cash deal. The acquisition is Uber’s latest move to grow its delivery business, which has become its fastest-growing major business segment. The deal will give Uber a bigger presence in the corporate food and catering market.
Uber is buying corporate catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion. (Representational Photo/REUTERS)
Founded in 2007, ezCater helps companies order food from caterers for office meetings, corporate events and workplace meals. Instead of ordering individual meals, businesses can use the platform to arrange large food orders for groups of employees or event attendees. Uber said ezCater generated more than $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the past 12 months, according to Reuters.
Corporate catering can bring Uber much larger orders than normal food deliveries. Uber said the average ezCater order is worth more than $400. This means one corporate order can be worth much more than a typical individual Uber Eats order. The deal also gives Uber a new business line based on large food orders paid for by companies, rather than individual customers.

The acquisition will bring together ezCater’s catering business, Uber Eats’ restaurant network and Uber for Business’ corporate customers, Uber said. This could allow Uber to offer companies a broader food-ordering service through its existing business network. Uber can use its existing restaurant and delivery infrastructure while ezCater brings its corporate catering business, according to Reuters.
The deal also strengthens Uber’s business-focused segment, which serves corporate customers. Gross bookings in this segment grew by more than 40% in the second quarter, according to Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt. Devitt said bringing workplace buyers into Uber’s ecosystem could also help strengthen its membership business.
Uber Eats has a larger global reach, but DoorDash remains the biggest player in the US food delivery market, according to analysts cited by Reuters. Buying ezCater could help Uber close some of that gap in the US. Corporate catering gives Uber another way to attract food-delivery customers beyond regular restaurant orders.

Uber said ezCater’s average order value is above $400. The company expects the acquisition to boost margins. Larger orders can make the delivery business more valuable because Uber can generate more business from each corporate transaction.
The ezCater deal comes only months after Uber agreed in July to buy German food-delivery company Delivery Hero for $14.8 billion. That deal is aimed at creating the largest food-delivery group outside China, according to Reuters. Together, the two deals show that Uber is putting significant money into expanding its delivery operations.
Uber’s delivery business accounted for about 37% of the company’s total revenue in the second quarter. It has also been Uber’s biggest growth driver in recent times. The ezCater acquisition therefore fits into Uber’s wider strategy of making delivery a bigger part of its business.
Uber’s shares have fallen about 15% this year as investors consider how the company will compete if robotaxis changes the ride-hailing industry. The possible rise of autonomous taxis could put pressure on Uber’s traditional ride-hailing business. Expanding food delivery and corporate services gives Uber another source of growth as the future of traditional ride-hailing becomes less certain.
The deal gives Uber access to a corporate catering platform that already handles billions of dollars in bookings. It adds high-value orders, brings more companies into Uber’s ecosystem and expands Uber’s business customer base. It also gives Uber another way to compete in the US food-delivery market while strengthening its fastest-growing business. The acquisition still needs regulatory approval. Uber expects the deal to close in the coming months, according to Reuters.

A discounted multiple against Uber's own history is not automatically a discount to its future obligations.

Stop Overpaying for Uber: How to Score Senior Discounts on Rideshare Apps
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:36 AM CDT 5 min read
A little more than a decade ago, getting into a stranger's car and telling them where to take you would be viewed as ill-advised at best. But with the rise of rideshare apps like Uber, Lyft and others, nothing seems more ordinary. The system comes with a lot of benefits; it tends to be cheaper than traditional taxis, it works effectively in most places and you can get practically wherever you want to go.
Combine the rideshare phenomenon with more traditional modes of transportation, and the world has gotten more mobile than ever before with plenty of options to travel. Alas, almost all those options still cost money. Luckily for seniors, there are also plenty of opportunities to save money while getting around.
Want more ways to save money? Sign up for The Penny Hoarder's free newsletter today.
How to Score Senior Discounts on Ridesharing Apps
The bigger rideshare companies all have their own apps, and if you know what to look for, there are loads of ways to save.
When using any of these apps, keep an eye out for promo codes that can help you save even more. In recent promotions, Lyft and Uber both advertise promo codes which give up to 50% discounts to new riders, regardless of your age.
Lyft doesn't offer a generalized senior discount for their basic service, but through their Lyft Silver program, seniors can use a simplified interface, find better vehicle matches (easier entry and exit) and get support to book their ride through Lyft.
Lyft's subscription service Lyft Pink does offer discounts with plans starting at $9.99 (or $99/year). For those who need to travel on a regular basis or have a busy schedule, Pink can help you save a bundle.
Additionally, many cities partner with Lyft to offer discounted rides to those 60 and older. In Charleston, South Carolina, CARTA offers seniors Lyft or Uber trips for as little as $5 each way within a fixed-route area.
Similar to Lyft, Uber doesn't offer a specific senior discount, but it does partner with municipalities to offer discounted rides for those 60 and older.
Also similar to Lyft, if you're a frequent rider, you can save money with a membership. An Uber One membership costs $9.99 (or $96/year) and lets you earn 5% back on rides and includes a $0 delivery fee for food and grocery orders.
GoGoGrandparent.com connects you to rideshare services and arranges deliveries of groceries and medications. Despite the name, anyone over 18 can order a ride and you can use it from any phone that generates tones by the press of a button — meaning, you don't need a smartphone. It features a simple menu and a live service that can help customers find the best and cheapest options. It also includes several financing options to help seniors save even more.
Memberships start at $15.58 for a Basic Plan (or $187/year). On top of helping connect people with rideshare services, GoGoGrandparent can connect you with delivery services for groceries, meals and prescriptions.
While it caters to families to with kids, HopSkipDrive.com provides transportation for anyone over the age of 6, and it's been expanding across the country. There are no upfront membership fees or monthly dues — you only pay for the rides you schedule. HopSkipDrive is a newer service and still expanding, so check out their website to see if your area is covered.
Another resource available to help senior citizens is NEMT (Non-Emergency Medical Transportation) programs, which provide free rides to medical appointments. Typically available through Medicaid and some Medicare Advantage plans, NEMT programs can be found in every state, including Alaska and Hawaii.
Seniors with visual impairment or mobility issues can also find free rides through ITNAmerica. The nonprofit transportation network helps seniors connect with free travel options through a variety of companies, ministries and charity organizations. You can find participating programs in your area at ridesinsight.org.
Other Ways Seniors Can Save on Transportation
For seniors still driving their own vehicle, AAA offers a variety of discounts and programs tailored to senior citizens, including discounts to 30,000 retailers. And if you haven't compared auto insurance rates lately, you could save hundreds of dollars.
Dial-a-ride programs can also be found across the country, usually managed by the same public transportation companies in your area. These programs, such as ACCESS LYNX in the Orlando area, work similarly to rideshare programs. They use shuttles to deliver customers to their chosen destinations, can schedule pick-up times and offer discounts for seniors.
When it comes to standard public transportation service, senior citizens can expect some form of discount. Buses, subways, trains and taxi services across the country usually offer senior discounts. Don't be afraid to ask about reduced fares.
If seniors are unable to drive, many local governments will offer free transportation as well. This will need official documents, such as a doctor's note and proof of income, but these programs are available in rural areas and urban centers across the country.

High Court dismisses £340m claims against Uber
Photo: HaeB / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
On 19 October 2026, Judge Simon Birt at the High Court dismissed two claims against Uber totaling about £340 million. About 13,000 black cab drivers sought nearly £200 million and a Kabbee and Iride claimant about £140 million. Filed in 2024, the suits alleged Uber misled Transport for London to obtain its 2012 private-hire licence and diverted business from traditional operators. Uber denied the allegations. Birt found the claimants had access by February 2018 to information that could have enabled a case and ruled the claims time-barred under the six-year limit. He did not decide whether the allegations were true.
An Uber spokesperson said the court dismissed all of the claims entirely at the earliest opportunity and put these legacy matters firmly in the past. RGL Management, running the claimants' case, said it was very disappointed and is considering all options available to the claimant cab drivers with the legal team. Mishcon de Reya notified Uber by letter in 2019 then went silent four and a half years after a litigation funder withdrew. Outlets differ on the headline sum, with some citing £250 million ($333 million) and others about $453 million. Uber faces a separate UK tax dispute of more than £1 billion in court the following week.

Early Uber Investor Jason Calacanis Predicts Waymo Could Buy Lucid Or Rivian — Calls Its Chinese-Car Optics ‘Really Bad’
Calacanis previously disclosed small investments in Lucid, Rivian, WeRide and Pony.ai, predicting takeovers within two years.
Jason Calacanis at The Besties All-In Tequila Launch Party at Delilah on June 21, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by JC Olivera/Variety via Getty Images)
Jason Calacanis predicted Waymo will buy Lucid or Rivian amid scrutiny of its Chinese-made robotaxi orders.
He called the Chinese-car optics “really bad,” citing tariffs, costs and national-security concerns.
U.S. vehicle restrictions begin phasing in with model year 2027, with certain hardware restrictions following in 2030.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Early Uber investor Jason Calacanis predicted that Alphabet’s Waymo will buy Lucid Group (LCID) or Rivian Automotive (RIVN), saying that its reliance on Chinese-made vehicles creates cost and reputational challenges as it expands its robotaxi fleet.
Calacanis Sees A Buyout To Waymo’s China Problem
ASTS Stock Jumps Overnight: CFO Gets New 3-Year Contract — Here’s What’s In His Pay And Exit Package
“They will buy Lucid or Rivian,” Calacanis said on X, while addressing Waymo’s vehicle sourcing and competition with Tesla. The development came after a New York Post report said that Waymo had ordered thousands of Chinese-made Zeekr vehicles to expand its U.S. fleet, drawing national-security concerns on Capitol Hill. Zeekr is part of China’s Geely group.
Calacanis said that tariffs and political concerns make the arrangement difficult to sustain. “Technically not illegal today, Waymo just needs to pay 100%+ tariff on these cars… but obviously something they need to deprecate because it’s not cost effective and the optics are really bad,” he said.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
“Even if the self-driving tech is from America, there will be reasonable concerns about communist rivals deploying AVs in America,” he added.
His acquisition prediction came after AI researcher Joscha Bach said that Waymo’s self-driving tech is fitted in the U.S. and added that the company lacks a domestic vehicle platform competitive with Tesla on cost.
Waymo has said its Ojai vehicle uses its sixth-generation Waymo Driver. The company is scaling vehicle integration at its Mesa, Arizona, factory toward capacity of tens of thousands of vehicles annually.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
U.S. vehicle rules restrict certain Chinese software and sales by Chinese-controlled vehicle manufacturers beginning with model year 2027. Restrictions on certain Chinese connectivity hardware begin with model year 2030, with authorization mechanisms available for otherwise prohibited transactions.
Calacanis Bets On Takeovers And 2x Return
Calacanis’s prediction comes after his disclosure from last month that he bought small positions in Lucid, Rivian and autonomous-driving companies WeRide (WRD) and Pony.ai (PONY). “Consolidation is coming to the autonomous space based on the massive progress that Tesla, Waymo, and Uber are making,” he said at the time.
“I believe these four companies are going to be bought in the next 24 months and I expect, as a group, that I will 2x my investment in under two years.” He also called the investments “tiny bets” with a one-to-four-year horizon.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Waymo Targets 20,000 Vehicles By End Of 2027
The prediction comes as Waymo apparently prepares for a huge expansion. The company wants to increase its fleet from about 4,000 vehicles to 8,000 by the end of 2026 and 20,000 by the end of 2027, Semafor reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Waymo closed its first debt financing, a $5 billion term loan, earlier this month after a $16 billion equity raise this year. The company said that the funds would support U.S. and international expansion after it launched service in its 15th U.S. city last month.
Lucid And Rivian Pursue Robotaxi Scale Through Uber
Uber has committed to buying at least 35,000 Lucid vehicles, including Gravity SUVs and future Midsize models, for a robotaxi service being developed with Nuro. It also pledged another $200 million in April, bringing its total investment commitments in Lucid to $500 million.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Lucid has a separate opportunity in Europe. Bolt said last month that it aims to put at least 25,000 autonomous vehicles based on Lucid’s upcoming Midsize platform into service.
Rivian’s Uber deal starts with 10,000 autonomous R2 SUVs, with rides expected to begin in San Francisco and Miami in 2028. The agreement includes an option for up to 40,000 more vehicles beginning in 2030. Uber also plans to invest up to $1.25 billion in Rivian through 2031, provided the automaker meets certain autonomy milestones.

Uber and Lyft Drivers in California Now Have a Gig Worker Rarity: A Union
Independent contractors, especially gig workers, aren’t generally afforded the rights and privileges of employees. Most don’t have access to healthcare, retirement plans — or unions. But that all changed recently for Uber and Lyft workers in California.
On Sept. 9, the California Public Employment Relations Board certified the California Gig Workers Union as the bargaining organization for drivers working for covered transportation network companies. For now, that means Uber and Lyft. Soon, drivers may be able to negotiate over pay and other working conditions.
Start Shopping: I'm an Auto Expert: These Used Cars Could Get Cheaper Throughout 2026
Earn Easily: 8 Low-Effort Ways To Make Passive Income (You Can Start This Week)
More Than 100,000 California Drivers Could Be Affected
The Transportation Network Company Drivers Labor Relations Act, which took effect Jan. 1, 2026, gives rideshare drivers the right to organize and bargain collectively while retaining their status as independent contractors.
For this all to happen, at least 30% of active drivers had to authorize the union to act as their bargaining representative. After reaching the 10% level in June, support topped the threshold required for certification by August. This led to formal certification by the PERB on Sept. 9.
The potential reach of the union is significant. As of the first half of 2026, PERB reported 100,307 active transportation network company drivers, with the vast majority working with Uber and Lyft. Those two companies alone accounted for more than 99% of the 75.2 million covered rides reported during that period.
A Union Doesn't Guarantee Drivers Higher Pay
A union might fight for workers’ rights, but it doesn’t mean the Uber and Lyft drivers will automatically get raises or new benefits. The ultimate financial effect on drivers, if any, will depend on the union’s course of action and what it can get companies to agree to.
If you’re considering taking a job as an Uber or Lyft driver because of the union news, be aware that the new union doesn’t guarantee higher pay or real benefits. Each bargaining proposal will be fought for by the union, but nothing goes into effect until an actual agreement is reached.
California Is Testing a Different Model for Gig Work
The bigger story may be the unusual combination California has created.
The state has traditionally separated independent contractors from traditional employees for legal purposes. But this new system allows drivers to remain independent contractors while still potentially benefitting from the collective bargaining rights of the union.
As this is all somewhat experimental, it’s worth watching to see how it all plays out in California and whether similar approaches succeed elsewhere in the country. A strong collective bargaining agreement for Uber and Lyft drivers could ultimately alter the economics of rideshare driving for people who rely on these gig jobs for either supplemental income or full-time earnings. Whether or not any agreements alter the pricing structure for riders is also a worthy consideration.
For the time being, nothing about a driver’s paycheck will change immediately simply because the union was certified. But with the earnings of more than 100,000 active California rideshare drivers potentially being affected, these new developments mark a significant change for one of America’s best-known gig-economy jobs.

FILE PHOTO: Uber Technologies has agreed to acquire US workplace catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion in an all-cash transaction to expand Uber Eats into group catering and workplace meals.
| Photo Credit:
Uber Technologies has agreed to acquire US workplace catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion in an all-cash transaction, as the ride-hailing and food delivery company seeks to expand Uber Eats into group catering and workplace meals.
Uber, in a press release on Tuesday, said that the acquisition will combine ezCater’s catering and business-to-business expertise with Uber Eats’ consumer and restaurant network and Uber for Business’ relationships with organisations, the companies said in a joint announcement.
ezCater enables businesses to order food from more than 140,000 restaurants across the US and manages workplace meals, meetings, events and recurring catering requirements. The platform generated more than $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the trailing 12 months, growing at a high-teens rate year-on-year.
The business is profitable on a non-GAAP operating income basis and is expected to be margin accretive to Uber, according to the companies. Its average order value exceeds $400, significantly positioning catering as a higher-value segment for restaurants and delivery partners.
Uber sees catering as a major revenue opportunity
“Catering is a big business, and can be a huge revenue stream for restaurants,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said, adding that Uber’s reach could bring ezCater’s catering experience to more customers and help restaurants capture more such orders.
The transaction is expected to provide restaurants with access to larger orders and new customers, while allowing consumers to order food for workplace gatherings, events and social occasions through a more integrated platform. Uber also expects the deal to create additional earning opportunities for its delivery couriers.
ezCater CEO Nihad Rahman said the company would bring its catering and B2B expertise into Uber’s broader ecosystem of customers, merchants and couriers.
Uber expands food delivery beyond individual meals
The acquisition comes as Uber looks to broaden its food delivery business beyond individual meal orders. By combining ezCater’s established workplace catering platform with Uber Eats’ existing consumer and restaurant reach, the company expects to expand access to group food orders while strengthening the value proposition for restaurant partners.
The transaction is expected to close in the coming months, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.
J.P. Morgan Securities is serving as financial adviser to Uber, while Evercore is advising ezCater. Covington & Burling and Freshfields US are providing legal counsel to Uber, while Davis Polk & Wardwell is advising ezCater.

Uber-ezCater deal: Why Uber is spending $2.3 billion on corporate catering
Uber will buy ezCater for $2.3 billion to expand corporate catering, grow Uber Eats and strengthen its delivery business with high-value orders.
Uber Technologies said on Tuesday that it will buy US corporate catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion in an all-cash deal. The acquisition is Uber’s latest move to grow its delivery business, which has become its fastest-growing major business segment. The deal will give Uber a bigger presence in the corporate food and catering market.
Uber is buying corporate catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion. (Representational Photo/REUTERS)
Founded in 2007, ezCater helps companies order food from caterers for office meetings, corporate events and workplace meals. Instead of ordering individual meals, businesses can use the platform to arrange large food orders for groups of employees or event attendees. Uber said ezCater generated more than $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the past 12 months, according to Reuters.
Corporate catering can bring Uber much larger orders than normal food deliveries. Uber said the average ezCater order is worth more than $400. This means one corporate order can be worth much more than a typical individual Uber Eats order. The deal also gives Uber a new business line based on large food orders paid for by companies, rather than individual customers.
Also read: Jim Bakker’s PTL Club: How a Christian TV show became a 13-million-viewer media empire
The acquisition will bring together ezCater’s catering business, Uber Eats’ restaurant network and Uber for Business’ corporate customers, Uber said. This could allow Uber to offer companies a broader food-ordering service through its existing business network. Uber can use its existing restaurant and delivery infrastructure while ezCater brings its corporate catering business, according to Reuters.
The deal also strengthens Uber’s business-focused segment, which serves corporate customers. Gross bookings in this segment grew by more than 40% in the second quarter, according to Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt. Devitt said bringing workplace buyers into Uber’s ecosystem could also help strengthen its membership business.
Uber Eats has a larger global reach, but DoorDash remains the biggest player in the US food delivery market, according to analysts cited by Reuters. Buying ezCater could help Uber close some of that gap in the US. Corporate catering gives Uber another way to attract food-delivery customers beyond regular restaurant orders.
Also read: Paramount-Warner merger: How Skydance plans to turn Hollywood into a tech company with AI and streaming
Uber said ezCater’s average order value is above $400. The company expects the acquisition to boost margins. Larger orders can make the delivery business more valuable because Uber can generate more business from each corporate transaction.
The ezCater deal comes only months after Uber agreed in July to buy German food-delivery company Delivery Hero for $14.8 billion. That deal is aimed at creating the largest food-delivery group outside China, according to Reuters. Together, the two deals show that Uber is putting significant money into expanding its delivery operations.
Uber’s delivery business accounted for about 37% of the company’s total revenue in the second quarter. It has also been Uber’s biggest growth driver in recent times. The ezCater acquisition therefore fits into Uber’s wider strategy of making delivery a bigger part of its business.
Uber’s shares have fallen about 15% this year as investors consider how the company will compete if robotaxis changes the ride-hailing industry. The possible rise of autonomous taxis could put pressure on Uber’s traditional ride-hailing business. Expanding food delivery and corporate services gives Uber another source of growth as the future of traditional ride-hailing becomes less certain.
The deal gives Uber access to a corporate catering platform that already handles billions of dollars in bookings. It adds high-value orders, brings more companies into Uber’s ecosystem and expands Uber’s business customer base. It also gives Uber another way to compete in the US food-delivery market while strengthening its fastest-growing business. The acquisition still needs regulatory approval. Uber expects the deal to close in the coming months, according to Reuters.

Uber Technologies (UBER) Is Generating Cash, but Can Robotaxi Spending Preserve Its Valuation?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:13 PM CDT 5 min read
Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) is approaching a difficult valuation test: its established ride-hailing network is producing more cash, while autonomous vehicles threaten to change who controls transportation demand. On September 2, the Financial Times reported plans to eliminate 3,300 corporate jobs, or about 10% of the global workforce, as the company redirects resources toward robotaxis. Analysts at Citi estimated roughly $825 million of annual savings. That would cover only a fraction of Uber's stated commitment of more than $10 billion to autonomous-vehicle expansion, so the investment case still turns on whether the new spending protects or dilutes future returns.
Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) reported more than $58 billion of second-quarter 2026 gross bookings, up 22% year-over-year, and revenue of $14.19 billion, up 12%. Trailing twelve-month free cash flow exceeded $10 billion for the first time. Those numbers show why investors cannot assess the robotaxi transition simply as an existential threat: Uber has an existing earnings engine capable of helping fund the change. But gross bookings are customer transaction value, not company revenue, and that distinction matters when forecasting how much incremental driverless demand Uber can monetize.
Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) sits on the second spot on our list of the 10 best undervalued stocks to buy now according to Reddit, ranked by second-quarter hedge fund holders. The ranking raises a useful comparison: why did an established mobility platform outrank eight other potential value opportunities when its most important competitive question remains unsettled?
Uber Technologies (UBER) Is Generating Cash, but Can Robotaxi Spending Preserve Its Valuation?
Uber Technologies, Inc.'s network could become more valuable if manufacturers and fleet owners use it to fill empty seats. Management said autonomous vehicles were operating through its platform in seven cities, with a goal of 15 by the end of 2026. In early deployments, Uber reported roughly 25 to 30 trips per vehicle per day, a utilization rate that is financially important because expensive fleets earn nothing while parked.
However, operators such as Alphabet's Waymo may eventually acquire riders directly. An autonomous fleet can also shift bargaining power away from millions of independent drivers toward a smaller set of well-capitalized suppliers. The regulatory emphasis on hybrid fleets, as described by the Financial Times on September 5, therefore has a commercial dimension. Our earlier examination of whether Uber's economic moat can survive the robotaxi transition explores the same question from the perspective of network effects and potential disintermediation.
A second expansion complicates the economics. Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) agreed to acquire Delivery Hero in a transaction valuing the business at approximately €13 billion, with closing expected in the second half of 2027. Management hopes to add $1.2 billion to Delivery Hero's operating profit through a combination of efficiency and cross-selling. Yet the acquired business is loss-making, and realizing revenue synergies across many markets is harder to verify than simply removing duplicated overhead.
The Seeking Alpha data shows Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) at 15.12 times trailing GAAP earnings and 21.81 times forward GAAP earnings; the comparable non-GAAP multiples are 24.00 and 20.65, respectively. The difference between forward GAAP and non-GAAP readings is a reminder that the definition of earnings materially changes the apparent valuation. On non-GAAP forward earnings, the multiple is around 30% below Uber's five-year average of 29.60, but still above the sector median of 18.86.
The earnings trajectory also resists a simplistic cheap-stock label. Seeking Alpha shows forward GAAP EPS growth of approximately negative 0.22%, even as forward EBITDA growth is 28.74% and expected three-to-five-year EPS compound growth reaches 27.30%. Those figures can coexist when accounting items and the time horizons differ, but the gap demands attention. A discounted multiple against Uber's own history is not automatically a discount to its future obligations.
There is also a question of cash availability. Our examination of Uber's growing insurance bill and whether operating cash can keep up distinguishes insurance reserves from unrestricted cash. That matters when future robotaxi capital requirements compete with insurance collateral, acquisitions, and repurchases. Management has described an intention to devote about half of free cash flow to buybacks.
Institutional Money Is Watching the Transition
Insider Monkey's Q2 2026 13F database counted 151 bullish hedge funds, down from 153 in Q1, suggesting a broadly stable but not strengthening institutional base. At September 30, 48.75 million shares were sold short, up from 45.12 million on August 31, equivalent to 2.48% of the float. Neither measure proves a specific view about autonomous vehicles, but the increase in short positions sits alongside the company's substantial investment commitments.
Wells Fargo raised its target to $92 from $89 on October 5 and maintained Overweight, identifying durable U.S. mobility trips growth in 2027 as important while Waymo scales. That is the relevant test: if trips, margins, and free cash flow hold up during deployment, the valuation gap to Uber Technologies, Inc.'s historical multiple could narrow. If billions in fleet spending produce limited incremental economics or direct robotaxi competition reduces platform relevance, today's forward earnings estimates could require revision. A separate analysis of what the market is actually pricing into Uber's robotaxi risk lays out why strong cash flow and a declining share price can coexist.

Uber Technologies (UBER) Launches Offsite Advertising Using Its First Party Data
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 5:18 PM CDT 3 min read
Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER) is partnering with TripleLift to extend Uber Advertising audiences beyond Uber's own apps.
The new offsite audience expansion product uses Uber's first party mobility and delivery data to target users across the open web.
This collaboration marks Uber Advertising's first effort to monetize its data as an external media targeting layer for advertisers.
Uber's offsite audience expansion launch with TripleLift only captures part of what this data shift could mean for investors. Our analysis turns up 1 warning sign for Uber Technologies as well.
This push into offsite ads is one example of a wider automation and data theme that other listed companies are also tied to, highlighted in 92 robotics and automation stocks.
NYSE:UBER Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Oct 2026
Uber Technologies now runs a global platform that connects riders, drivers, couriers, and restaurants across multiple regions, which gives it a large stream of first party mobility and delivery data. That data sits alongside the core transportation apps and is now being applied to digital advertising decisions beyond its own ecosystem.
3 things going right for Uber Technologies that this headline doesn't cover.
Uber Technologies offsite ads plug straight into its high-intent data story
The investment story on Uber Technologies leans on using a huge pool of mobility and delivery activity to support more profitable revenue streams. This offsite partnership with TripleLift taps exactly that idea by exporting Uber Advertising audiences across the wider internet rather than keeping them confined to its own apps.
What the Uber Technologies Narrative says this data move really matters for
At heart, the Uber Technologies Narrative is a bet that heavy spending on memberships, autonomous vehicles and ancillary services will turn today's global ride and delivery footprint into better unit economics. This advertising move tests whether all that first party data can pull its weight beyond rides and food orders.
The main thing that has to go right is that Uber turns heavy spending on autonomous vehicles, membership, AV labs and large-scale integrations such as Delivery Hero into durable unit economics...
See how the full story points towards a $101 fair value for Uber Technologies.
This TripleLift tie up plugs directly into the catalyst about higher margin ancillary revenue like ads and Uber One. Instead of only monetising riders and eaters on in app real estate, Uber can now sell audience segments across the open web. That pushes the same data and user intent into a broader media budget conversation with brands that already buy from Meta and Alphabet.
There is a flip side that many headlines will skip over. Leaning harder on granular mobility and purchase data raises privacy, regulatory and brand safety questions that sit close to the Narrative's risk around complexity and oversight, especially as Uber also integrates Delivery Hero and AV labs data. For you as an investor, stitching this type of news into a consistent Narrative is what turns product updates into a view on the business.

Will Uber (UBER) Beat Estimates Again in Its Next Earnings Report?

Looking for a stock that has been consistently beating earnings estimates and might be well positioned to keep the streak alive in its next quarterly report? Uber Technologies (UBER), which belongs to the Zacks Internet - Services industry, could be a great candidate to consider.
This ride-hailing company has an established record of topping earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The company boasts an average surprise for the past two quarters of 21.91%.
For the most recent quarter, Uber was expected to post earnings of $0.83 per share, but it reported $1.17 per share instead, representing a surprise of 40.96%. For the previous quarter, the consensus estimate was $0.7 per share, while it actually produced $0.72 per share, a surprise of 2.86%.
Thanks in part to this history, there has been a favorable change in earnings estimates for Uber lately. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the stock is positive, which is a great indicator of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with its solid Zacks Rank.
Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.
The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.
Uber currently has an Earnings ESP of +7.78%, which suggests that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This positive Earnings ESP when combined with the stock's Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) indicates that another beat is possibly around the corner. We expect the company's next earnings report to be released on November 4, 2026.
Investors should note, however, that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss, but a negative value does reduce the predictive power of this metric.
Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER) ranks fourth on our list of President Trump and Nancy Pelosi Portfolio: Top 4 Picks. Bill Ackman's Pershing Square holds the stock too, and we covered the two stocks that Nancy Pelosi and Bill Ackman are both betting on.
What Uber Reported in the Latest Quarter
Uber reported its second-quarter results in August. Gross bookings grew 22% year over year, the fourth straight quarter above 20%. Delivery and Freight bookings each grew 25%, and Mobility bookings grew 20%. Non-GAAP earnings per share rose 35%, and trailing 12-month free cash flow hit a record. Shares fell after the report because the third-quarter earnings outlook came in a few cents below expectations.
Uber has a demand advantage because more than 200 million people use its app each month. That is why bulls think autonomous vehicles will end up as Uber partners. Uber already has deals with more than a dozen AV companies. Delivery gives it a second source of growth, and the pending Delivery Hero acquisition brings in a market leader in the Middle East, Latin America and Asia Pacific.

The biggest risk is that robotaxi operators become rivals. Waymo, Zoox and Tesla all run their own services, and Waymo's three-year Phoenix partnership through Uber's app ended in mid-2026. If the large operators keep their cars off Uber's app, the company may need a new plan for autonomous rides. Lower robotaxi prices could also pressure Uber's human-driver model. Videos of Tesla Cybercabs hailing rides on their own set off alarm bells in September. See which insider trades to watch after the Cybercab scare.
Uber trades at about 21 times forward non-GAAP earnings. That is below its five-year average of about 30 times and a little above the sector median of about 19 times. Analysts expect earnings per share to grow about 30% in 2026 and 42% in 2027. The forward PEG ratio, which pairs the P/E with growth, is 0.76 against a sector median of 1.46. Analyst consensus rates the stock a Buy. Montaka Global Investments bought Uber after a pullback in the first quarter. Read their thesis here.
Can Uber Keep Growing?
Analysts expect Uber to keep growing earnings at a fast pace through 2027, and gross bookings have grown more than 20% for four straight quarters. The answer depends on whether the large robotaxi operators keep using Uber's app. Management expects to announce a new AV partner for the Phoenix market soon, and that deal will show how much leverage Uber has. Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER) has the rider base that robotaxi makers need, and the next few partner deals will show whether that is enough.
