Teradyne Strengthens Pre-Shipment Testing for AI Semiconductors
U.S.-based Teradyne announced that it has enhanced reliability testing for AI semiconductor equipment.
The company aims to achieve both quality and production efficiency through per-chip temperature control and test history tracking.
A hint for work: in addition to asking "is it finished?", ask "have I verified it under the conditions in which it will be used?"
In discussions about AI, attention often turns to the semiconductors that perform calculations or the convenient services they power. Behind the scenes, U.S.-based Teradyne is a company that handles the equipment used to verify whether these semiconductors function as expected.
On October 6, 2026 (local time), the company announced that it has enhanced the burn-in functionality of its semiconductor test equipment, the "Titan HP." Burn-in is a test that verifies component reliability by applying loads such as temperature and power. [1]
The equipment itself was already announced in October 2025. [3] The news this time lies in the fact that the reliability testing capabilities of the existing equipment have been strengthened. The company explains that the enhanced version has begun shipping and is already being used on production floors. [1]
Regarding conventional methods, the company explains that the process involves managing the ambient air temperature in a dedicated oven for a certain period before proceeding to verify functionality.
With the Titan HP, the internal temperature of each chip is maintained at a target value while running processes close to actual usage. The concept is to verify the chip by combining operation and temperature to approximate the conditions during real-world use.
According to the product page, the entire system can continue to operate even while individual test sites are being serviced. The load and test history for each component are also consolidated into a single record. This is a mechanism that allows for tracking what was verified and under what conditions. [2]
What can be expected and what remains unknown
The company states that this can reduce inspection costs and floor space, as well as shorten the time to market for products. This is the expectation presented by the company. This announcement does not include specific comparative results, such as by what percentage costs were reduced or how much the failure rate improved. [1]
Furthermore, one cannot judge that the same effect will be achieved for all customers based solely on the explanation that it is "being used on production floors." The actual effect must be viewed in the context of the items being inspected and the operational conditions.
In corporate news, it is easier to understand if one separates the fact that a product has been released from the results expected thereafter. It is also important not to interpret the announcement of a new feature directly as an increase in sales or profits.
What can be gleaned from this announcement is that making quality verification easier to incorporate into daily tasks is also a form of product value. This is an interpretation based on the content of the announcement.
For example, a business tool that works with a small amount of data might produce different results during concentrated end-of-month processing. Even if a procedure manual is easy for the creator to understand, it may be difficult for someone handling it for the first time. The significance of adding the perspective of "how it is actually used" to the verification of completion applies to more than just semiconductors.

BOXBOROUGH, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct 14, 2026--
TÜV Rheinland North America presented Teradyne with their Excellence in Safety and Sustainability Leadership Award at their Oktoberfest Client Appreciation Event on September 17, 2026. The award recognizes customers in good standing that demonstrate leadership in safety, innovation, standards of compliance, employee training, and publicly declared sustainability initiatives.

Teradyne was selected based on strong documented alignment with the award criteria. An evidence-based review of Teradyne’s public disclosures found strong support for five key areas: commitment to safety, innovative safety programs and technologies, documented safety training systems, consistent standards compliance, and quantifiable sustainability commitments.
The review highlighted Teradyne’s companywide EHS audits, mandatory employee safety training, contractor safety requirements, product-safety governance, and technologies such as collaborative robots, autonomous mobile robots, telemetry, and predictive maintenance that help reduce worker exposure to repetitive, dangerous, and vehicle-related risks.
Teradyne’s sustainability progress also contributed to the recognition. Publicly reported results showed that its waste-recycling rate increased from 40% to 89% between 2021 and 2024, recycled material rose from 340 to 4,076 tons, and water consumption declined from 140,536 to 108,459 cubic meters. The review also cited annual CDP reporting, an SBTi commitment, and third-party limited assurance of Teradyne’s 2024 Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions inventory.
Under the award program, nominations are submitted by TÜV Rheinland North America by sales or field leadership and evaluated by a panel of three to five experts using predefined weighted criteria to ensure transparency and integrity in the selection process. Teradyne is the second annual winner of this award following the inaugural winner P&G.
With this award, TÜV Rheinland North America recognizes Teradyne’s leadership in advancing safer workplaces, safer technologies, and measurable sustainability performance.

The facility will support device evaluation, engineering development, pilot production, and training at GSME’s Silicon Valley headquarters.
GS Microelectronics U.S., Inc. and Teradyne, Inc. announced a multi‑year strategic partnership to establish a state‑of‑the‑art semiconductor test and evaluation center designed to accelerate customer time‑to‑market. The collaboration integrates GSME’s turnkey design and manufacturing enablement capabilities with Teradyne’s industry‑leading automated test platforms, creating a high‑performance environment for device evaluation, engineering development, and production readiness.
GSME-Teradyne Partnership.
Under the agreement, GSME will operate a dedicated Teradyne‑equipped test floor and provide hands‑on engineering support for customers developing next‑generation devices across AI, silicon photonics, automotive, power management, RF technologies, and other emerging semiconductor applications.
State‑of‑the‑Art test center and infrastructure
GSME will deploy Teradyne’s most advanced test systems within a dedicated test facility located at its new 42,000 square-foot Silicon Valley headquarters. The center will support customer demonstrations, device evaluations, engineering development, pilot production, and technical training, utilizing the latest test handlers and probers.
GSME is expanding its global team of highly qualified test engineers across the United States, Taiwan, Europe and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region to support customers, design‑in engagements, test program development, and customer‑specific application requirements.
GSME and Teradyne will collaborate through joint sales engagements, target account development, technical workshops, and customer briefings to accelerate Teradyne‑based design wins and broaden market adoption.
The test center is scheduled to open at GSME’s Silicon Valley headquarters in Q4 2026, with customer demonstrations and evaluations beginning shortly thereafter.
For more information, visit gsme.com.

What Happened?
A number of stocks fell in the morning session after hotter-than-expected inflation data compounded fears that elevated borrowing costs will curb artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.
The sell-off followed a Bureau of Labor Statistics release showing September wholesale prices climbed 1.3%, marking a 6.3% annual advance that outpaced the 5.5% projection from economists polled by Dow Jones. Compounding an above-forecast consumer price print from the prior session, the hotter CPI inflation reading drove the 10-year Treasury yield past 5.27%, based on CNBC market data. However, rates cooled off a bit in the pre market session.Higher benchmark rates threaten the debt-heavy funding required to power data center expansion. Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives observed in a client note carried by CNBC that while compute demand remains sound, climbing yields directly inflate project financing costs and intensify scrutiny on balance sheets.
Semiconductor valuations reflect aggressive, uninterrupted capital spending from cloud hyperscalers. When capital costs stay elevated, the payback timeline on multi-billion-dollar clusters lengthens, raising the hurdle rate for new hardware commitments and delaying order realization across the component supply chain.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

TÜV Rheinland North America Honors Teradyne with 2026 Excellence in Safety and Sustainability Leadership Award
TÜV Rheinland presents the 2026 Excellence in Safety and Sustainability Leadership Award to Teradyne. Pictured from left to right: Kimmo Fuller and Steve Niernberg (TÜV Rheinland), Brad Bombardier (Teradyne), and Jonathan Kotrba (TÜV Rheinland).
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 7:16 AM CDT 2 min read
BOXBOROUGH, Mass., October 14, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--TÜV Rheinland North America presented Teradyne with their Excellence in Safety and Sustainability Leadership Award at their Oktoberfest Client Appreciation Event on September 17, 2026. The award recognizes customers in good standing that demonstrate leadership in safety, innovation, standards of compliance, employee training, and publicly declared sustainability initiatives.
Teradyne was selected based on strong documented alignment with the award criteria. An evidence-based review of Teradyne's public disclosures found strong support for five key areas: commitment to safety, innovative safety programs and technologies, documented safety training systems, consistent standards compliance, and quantifiable sustainability commitments.
The review highlighted Teradyne's companywide EHS audits, mandatory employee safety training, contractor safety requirements, product-safety governance, and technologies such as collaborative robots, autonomous mobile robots, telemetry, and predictive maintenance that help reduce worker exposure to repetitive, dangerous, and vehicle-related risks.
Teradyne's sustainability progress also contributed to the recognition. Publicly reported results showed that its waste-recycling rate increased from 40% to 89% between 2021 and 2024, recycled material rose from 340 to 4,076 tons, and water consumption declined from 140,536 to 108,459 cubic meters. The review also cited annual CDP reporting, an SBTi commitment, and third-party limited assurance of Teradyne's 2024 Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions inventory.

AI Chips Need Testing, and Teradyne (TER) Is Winning. Is the Valuation Too High?
Robots get the headlines at Teradyne (NASDAQ:TER). Chip testers pay the bills. In the second quarter of 2026, the company's robotics arm brought in $100 million. Its semiconductor test business brought in $1.12 billion over the same three months.
That split matters, because the stock isn't cheap. Teradyne builds the machines that check chips for defects before they ship, a step every AI processor and memory chip has to clear. It also owns Universal Robots, a maker of collaborative robot arms (cobots, built to work beside people) found on factory floors around the world. That operational momentum earns the stock a spot among the 10 High-Beta Stocks with Strong Revenue Growth. So what are investors actually paying for at 44 times expected earnings? The answer depends less on the robots than on how long the testing boom lasts.
AI Chips Need Testing, and Teradyne (TER) Is Winning. Is the Valuation Too High?
The second quarter was Teradyne's second straight record. Revenue hit $1.33 billion, up 104% from $652 million a year earlier, and beat the top of management's own guidance. Adjusted (non-GAAP) earnings per share came in at $2.47, against $0.57 a year before.
Memory was a big driver. Teradyne posted record memory revenue on continued DRAM strength and a revival in NAND final test, the last check flash chips get before shipping. The AI build-out is clearly pulling on more than just processors; a tailwind memory chipmakers like Micron are riding too.
Pricing power shows up in the margins. Gross margin came in at 59.8%, and CEO Greg Smith said rising wafer fab equipment spending sets the company up for growth in 2027 and beyond.
Robotics is small, but it's no longer just about arms. At the Automate trade show earlier this year, Teradyne Robotics showed off what it calls production-ready physical AI, robots that adapt to messy surroundings instead of repeating one motion. Its first physical AI product, the MiR1200 Pallet Jack, is already for sale.
The more telling detail was who else showed up. Partners demonstrated AI bin picking from Vention, imitation-learning tools built with Scale AI, and dual-arm robots threading copper cables into server racks, all running on Universal Robots hardware. Teradyne also taps Nvidia's GR00T model and Isaac Sim simulation software. When outside developers build on your arms, the platform starts to look like a standard, which keeps Teradyne in the conversation about robotics stocks betting on physical AI.
Has the Testing Cycle Peaked?
Here's the worry. Teradyne guided third-quarter revenue to $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion, below the record $1.33 billion it posted in the second quarter. Adjusted EPS guidance of $1.85 to $2.15 also sits under the second quarter's $2.47. Gross margin had already slipped to 59.8% from 60.9% in the first quarter.
Chip testing has always been cyclical, and a step down after a record can be the first sign of a plateau. Robotics, at $100 million a quarter, is far too small to cushion a semiconductor slowdown. Management's guidance still credits strong AI-related demand, though, and its 2027 outlook doesn't read like a company bracing for a bust. One softer quarter wouldn't break the story. Two in a row would, leaving valuation-conscious investors looking elsewhere, as Teradyne misses out on the 10 Best Affordable Stocks to Buy According to Wall Street Analysts.
At 44.29 times forward earnings, as of October 12, Teradyne trades well above the sector's 23.29. It also sits above its own five-year average of 35.27, so investors are paying up even by Teradyne's standards.
Growth is the defense. Analysts expect earnings to grow 28.17% in 2027. That's fast, but it doesn't fully explain a multiple this far above the stock's own history. The price assumes AI testing demand keeps rolling for years and that robotics eventually becomes a real earnings contributor rather than a side story. It's the same tension running through AI chip equipment stocks, where booming orders meet stretched multiples.
Short interest sits at 6.38% of the float, meaning a noticeable slice of traders is betting the rally has gone too far. Hedge funds moved the other way, with 82 holding the stock in the most recent quarter, up from 80 in the prior one.
The evidence says investors are paying for the testing boom, with robotics as an option on top. That boom is real, and the 2027 growth forecast gives the premium some cover. The setup suits growth investors who can stomach chip-cycle swings and believe AI test demand lasts into 2027. If the third quarter lands inside guidance and management holds its 2027 view, 44 times earnings looks defensible. A second straight sequential decline, or fading memory strength, would make it look like peak pricing.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of TER as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than TER and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock.

Investing.com -- FormFactor Inc (NASDAQ:FORM) shares rose 3.6% in after-hours trading Monday following the announcement of a strategic technology collaboration with Teradyne Inc (NASDAQ:TER) and a $300 million equity investment from the automated test equipment provider.

The partnership brings together FormFactor's probe technologies and interface solutions with Teradyne's automated test platforms to address semiconductor testing challenges. The collaboration will focus on advancing test architectures for high-performance compute, advanced packaging, high-bandwidth memory, and silicon photonics applications.
Under the agreement, Teradyne will purchase $300 million in FormFactor common stock. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

FormFactor, based in Livermore, California, provides semiconductor test and measurement technologies. The company's expertise includes probe technologies, interface solutions, test engineering, and device characterization.
"The semiconductor industry is entering a period where test performance, scalability, and time-to-market are becoming decisive competitive advantages," said Mike Slessor, Chief Executive Officer of FormFactor. "By combining FormFactor's deep expertise in device characterization, probing, interfaces, and production test solutions with Teradyne's test platforms, we can help customers accelerate innovation and move more efficiently from technology development to high-volume manufacturing."
Gregory Smith, President and Chief Executive Officer of Teradyne, commented: "The most demanding test challenges in advanced packaging, silicon photonics, and memory can't be solved by a single company. By investing in FormFactor and combining our leading-edge test platforms with FormFactor's probe and interface expertise, we're building a more complete, validated path to production for our shared customers, and reinforcing our commitment to an open, interoperable ecosystem."
The companies said the collaboration will support joint customer engagement and address demand for advanced computing and AI infrastructure.

Teradyne Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
Second consecutive quarter of record revenue, exceeding the high end of our Q2 Guidance
Revenue up 104% and earnings up over 300% from Q2’25
Record Memory revenue driven by continued strength in DRAM and a resurgence in NAND final test
NORTH READING, Mass. – July 28, 2026 – Teradyne, Inc. (NASDAQ: TER) reported revenue of $1,329 million for the second quarter of 2026 of which $1,122 million was in Semiconductor Test, $107 million in Product Test, and $100 million in Robotics. On a GAAP-basis, net income attributable to Teradyne for the second quarter of 2026 was $374.5 million, or $2.38 per diluted share. On a non-GAAP basis, net income attributable to Teradyne for the second quarter of 2026 was $389.0 million, or $2.47 per diluted share, which excluded acquired intangible asset amortization, restructuring and other charges, and the related tax impact on non-GAAP adjustment.
"Our strategy to capture test and robotics opportunities from wafer to AI data center has driven another record quarter. This strength became evident in the year-on-year market expansion for all three of our business groups,” said Teradyne CEO Greg Smith. “In the short term, our Q3 guidance reflects robust AI-related demand. Looking further ahead, rapid increase in wafer fab equipment investment sets the stage for continued growth in 2027 and beyond."
Guidance for the third quarter of 2026 is revenue of $1,200 million to $1,300 million, with GAAP net income attributable to Teradyne of $1.79 to $2.09 per diluted share and non-GAAP net income attributable to Teradyne of $1.85 to $2.15 per diluted share. Non-GAAP guidance excludes acquired intangible asset amortization and amortization on our investment in Technoprobe, as well as the related tax impact on non-GAAP adjustments.
A conference call to discuss the second quarter results, along with management’s business outlook, will follow at 8:30 a.m. ET, July 29, 2026. Interested investors should access the webcast at www.teradyne.com and click on “Investors” at least five minutes before the call begins. Presentation materials will be available starting at 7:30 a.m. ET. A replay will be available on the Teradyne website at www.teradyne.com/investors.
In addition to disclosing results that are determined in accordance with GAAP, Teradyne also discloses non-GAAP results of operations that exclude certain income items and charges. These results are provided as a complement to results provided in accordance with GAAP. Non-GAAP income from operations and non-GAAP net income attributable to Teradyne excludes acquired intangible assets amortization, restructuring and other, ERP related expenses, inventory step-up, pension mark-to-market adjustment, pension actuarial gains and losses, discrete income tax adjustments, and the related tax impact on non-GAAP adjustments. GAAP requires that these items be included in determining income from operations and net income. Non-GAAP income from operations, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP income from operations as a percentage of revenue, non-GAAP net income as a percentage of revenue, and non-GAAP net income per share are non-GAAP performance measures presented to provide meaningful supplemental information regarding Teradyne’s baseline performance before gains, losses or other charges that may not be indicative of Teradyne’s current core business or future outlook. These non-GAAP performance measures are used to make operational decisions, to determine employee compensation, to forecast future operational results, and for comparison with Teradyne’s business plan, historical operating results and the operating results of Teradyne’s competitors. Management believes each of these non-GAAP performance measures provides useful supplemental information for investors, allowing greater transparency to the information used by management in its operational decision making and in the review of Teradyne’s financial and operational performance, as well as facilitating meaningful comparisons of Teradyne’s results in the current period compared with those in prior and future periods.
